platform_aggregate_ratings.notes: Different Shiksha page snapshots retrieved at different times showed 749, 809, 849, 851, 866 as review_count — these are the same live counter changing over time / across page variants, not independent counts. Reporting most recent observed value; backend should treat this as a single time-varying aggregate, not multiple data points.
Site-wide review_count not confirmable — mirrored subdomains (s2/s3/s4.collegedunia.com) returned the same rating (7.9) without a consistent visible total count in accessible snippets.
This is a course-level (B.Arch) rating, not the institution-wide rating. Kept separate per instruction to preserve branch/course granularity.

Page also displays a platform-computed 'Rating Summary' breakdown (Infrastructure 3.6/5, Academics 3.7/5, Placements 3.9/5, Value for Money 3.2/5, Campus Life 4.3/5). These are Careers360's own aggregate sub-scores, not derived by me — reported as observed, not recalculated.

This Collegedunia mirror displayed a 5-point scale (3.9/5) rather than the 10-point scale (7.9/10) seen on the main collegedunia.com page, with sub-ratings Academic 4.0, Faculty 4.0, Infrastructure 3.5, Accommodation 4.0, Placement 4.0. This may be a legacy/alternate rating widget on the same platform. Reported as-observed; not reconciled with the 7.9/10 figure — flagging discrepancy for backend review rather than resolving it myself.

review_items.evidence_summary: 53 offers, ~48 students placed (~84.21%), average package 7.63 LPA, highest 18.45 LPA by BPCL — described positively. For electrical branch specifically: 'no upgraded machinery and equipment available... too risky to work on those,' placement lab computers 'not in working condition' — infrastructure described negatively.

Mechanical intake 210 students; average package ~8.5 LPA prior year; Bajaj and Hero cited as frequent recruiters; HPCL and Vedanta offered ~14 LPA to 14+ students recently. Reviewer name: Sree Dharan (attributed in source, but branch/course label for this specific reviewer was ambiguous in the snippet — treating as Mechanical based on content).

Reviewer: Mayank Aggarwal, Batch of 2013. 'CSE and mechanical rated 8/10 for infrastructure' but electrical branch has no upgraded machinery. Hostels 8,9,10 are newly built with modern amenities; other hostels 'belong to 1970s era.' Wi-Fi and digital library available. Placements described as 'good at that time.'

Reviewer: Pranjal Srivastava, Batch of 2029. 'Placements are quite decent. Placements can be better for core branches.' Faculty: 'highly qualified and very helpful.' Mechanical branch called 'famous for rich curriculum,' makes 'students industry-ready.'
'Faculty members are very good.' Exams described as 'a little tougher comparatively' with pass percentage 40-50%, relative grading system. Life at MANIT described as 'really fun and enthusiastic.'

Amazon, Goldman Sachs, Google cited as recruiters; average CSE package ~10-12 LPA, highest 64 LPA; placement rate ~70%. Infrastructure: 'average,' labs have 'old technology' equipment, high-speed Wi-Fi/LAN present, 7 canteens, gym, cricket ground. Faculty: autonomous institution, faculty design own syllabus, all faculty PhD.

Placements: 80-85% placed, packages 5-16 LPA, average ~8.5 LPA, recruiters Suzuki/Honda/Tata, ~30% got internships. Infrastructure: 'all labs available,' 'super fast' Wi-Fi, digital library, decent classrooms with projectors/mics. Campus life: 'could be better,' lush green campus underutilized for buildings. Scholarships called 'easy to access.'

Batch of 2024. Maximum package in civil 24 LPA. Placement percentage cited as 70%; remaining 30% reported wanting to work in core companies rather than being unplaced — described as 'placement is best' by reviewer despite the 70% figure, indicating a subjectively positive framing of a moderate number.

Placement percentage 'up to 90%,' highest package 82 LPA, average 15-17 LPA, recruiters Microsoft/Oracle/Amazon. Infrastructure: classrooms/labs/central library 'very well designed,' green/'pure' environment. Campus has 'good connectivity,' 'many societies for extracurricular activities.'

'This college is not as good as expected.' 75-80 seniors placed, highest 18 LPA, lowest 4.5 LPA. 'In the last 2-3 years, there have been some placement issues. Many seniors are not placed through campus recruitment and try to get jobs off campus.' Only 10-15% of seniors got internships.

Reviewer: Swayam jat, Ph.D CSE, review titled 'Limited career opportunities.' Infrastructure 'average but functional.' Academics 'average,' more practical exposure requested. Placements: 'number of companies and available roles could be improved.' Value for money: 'average.' Campus life: 'average, but enjoyable.'

Reviewer: YOGRAJ TANDON, review titled 'Mesmerising.' Robotics lab and computing facilities praised. Academic workshops/labs described positively. Placements: 'ECE has got down' but 'CSE and MDS are outstanding'; companies named: Google, Microsoft, Atlassian, Nvidia, Qualcomm; mechanical/electrical also described as having 'good placement stats.'

Reviewer: Anshul Gupta, review titled 'Study hard and come here fast,' marked Verified Review. Infrastructure: 'basic but enough' (night canteens, bus, hostels). Academics: 'quality of teaching is good but it could have been even better.' Placements: 'best in giving placement,' Mechanical average package 9-10 LPA, 'vast alumni network.'

Reviewer: Disha Kanjani, review titled 'Easy Campus life,' marked Verified Review. Infrastructure: 'old buildings, many cracks' contrasted with 'nature parks and forest area.' Academics/faculty: 'faculties are really really good.' Placements: 'NIT level' overall but 'in architecture there are no company' though 'some architecture firms pick up students,' highest package in tech branches up to 20-25 lakhs (not architecture-specific).

Anonymous reviewer, review titled 'Great academics and placements, but average infrastructure,' marked Verified Review, self-rated 3-star infrastructure. 'Aesthetic appeal leaves a lot to be desired... older buildings, mess halls, and hostels feel quite weathered.' Academics called 'genuinely one of its strongest assets.' Placements: 'honestly pretty great,' 'big tech giants and reputable core companies visit regularly.'

Anonymous reviewer, review titled 'A good college with lots of opportunities,' marked Verified Review. Infrastructure: 'quite good... huge green campus, well-equipped labs' but 'some hostel buildings and facilities feel a bit old.' Academics: 'decent overall... teaching quality depends a lot on the professor.' Placements: 'decent,' 'not outstanding for every branch.' Value for money: 'good... reasonable for an NIT.' Campus life: 'okayish overall.'

Reviewer: Raghvendra Singh Garhwal, review titled 'Giving a review to my college is quite good.' Infrastructure: 'buildings are really really old, need reconstruction... no proper ceiling' in NTB first floor, though 'most of the facilities' (bus, hostel, mess) present. Faculty: 'one of the finest in India,' experience teaching at IITs. Placements/internships: seniors placed at Google, Microsoft; internships in 3rd year at 'FAANG & MAANG.'

Reviewer: Chayan Jariwala, review titled 'National Institute with Cool Culture.' Infrastructure: buses/hostel/water cooler present but 'quality is not being checked,' 'buildings are very old and need renovation,' Wi-Fi 'not at high speed but still available.' Academics: called 'great,' resources 'upto the mark.' Placements: 'bit good,' mechanical gets 'basic enough salary,' CSE gets 'highest placement with avg package upto 25 to 30 LPA.'

Reviewer: Shreyashi kesharwani, review titled 'Amazing college and superb life living here.' Infrastructure: 'not so good... buildings are old,' but 'new department buildings' (vehicle engineering) built 'in modern way.' Academics: 'good,' opportunity to propose designs in 'L.I.K.' Placements: architecture placement 'very good... even in architecture some companies give placement which is very rare,' tech placements 'up to 20-25 lakhs.' Value for money and campus life (fests, clubs, 'Mafick events') described positively.

Reviewer: Shubham Atram, marked Verified Review, self-rated overall '9/10.' Infrastructure: 'needs to be re-designed,' buildings 'from 1990s,' 'many cracks in the walls,' tin-shed ceiling in NTB. Academics: 'really good,' professors with IIT Bombay teaching experience. Placements: CSE average package cited as 25 LPA, recruiters Google/Microsoft/Goldman Sachs. Campus life: auditoriums, parks, 650-acre wildlife area.

Enrolled 2024. 'Campus is in the city, connectivity is very good... It is the old campus, MANIT have very good alumni network and Bhopal is city of lake.' 'MANIT offered the best combination of ranking, location, branch preference, and return on investment.'
Enrolled 2024. 'Chose this campus only because it has very huge campus and good placements... startup culture is very good... sports complex has all the facilities.'

Enrolled 2020, JEE Main score 23000. 'Facilities in MANIT are highly qualified and have their PhD degree from reputed NITs, professors are highly knowledgeable on their subjects.' (Note: reviewer says 'facilities' but content describes faculty qualifications — classified under faculty based on described content.)

'Hostel facility are not good satisfying... 3 members in the room... food is not so good... sometimes get spoiled, sometimes water, electricity problems.' 'I disliked the ragging held here so its negative vibe of the college.' Placements described positively elsewhere in same aggregated snippet: 60+ lakh highest package, 85-90% placement rate.

'I like the hostel culture of the colleges as there are different types of people coming from different places of India.' 'I dislike the culture of ragging in the college and the senior junior behaviour.' Placement: 'quite good,' MAANG companies visit, packages 'up to 85 lac per annum,' 90% placement in reviewer's branch (avg 10 LPA); internship available by third year.

Ph.D scholar review titled 'Best college from my experience.' 'Provides Ph.D. scholars with a conducive infrastructure environment, academic support, as well as plentiful research opportunities... robust internet connectivity, dedicated research laboratories, central library with journal subscriptions to IEEE and ScienceDirect.'

Review titled 'Great atmosphere with a multitude of personalities.' 'Academic buildings and labs are well equipped for the most part. Every equipment works but the usage is very limited. Instead of the smart board being used for a deeper dive..., it ended up being used to put up premade slides from a few years back by the teachers (2 teachers to be specific in Civil Engineering department). But there are others as well that use it well.'

review_items.evidence_summary: Reviewer: Samyak jain, Enrolled 2022. 'From 7th semester students become eligible for campus placement and from 5th semester students become eligible for campus internship. Companies visited: Google, Microsoft, Texas, Bajaj, Flipkart, Oracle... highest package 80 LPA, average 24 LPA (CSE, software engineer profile), 98% placement percentage.'
Identical content to the s4 mirror listed above — same reviewer name, same date, same figures. Counted once in items_analyzed; this instance excluded from independent-item counting.

'For architecture MANIT is not so good as placement scenario is going worse day by day but faculty as well as facilities are at par level so if you are not concerned about placements then go for MANIT otherwise I suggest SPA Delhi.'

'Placements are quite good. In fact chemical engineering takes third place in college for placements after CSE and ECE department. The average package last year was 6-7 lakh and highest was around 21 lakhs.'

'Newer/upgraded programs: Data Science/AI, Cybersecurity... introduced or expanded since 2022. Faculty profile: growing proportion of PhD-holding faculty, several recent hires with industry or international experience. Administrative processes: occasional bureaucratic delays reported by students; improving digitalisation has reduced some friction.' Recommends MANIT for 'solid placements (especially CSE/ECE), active student life, and growing research opportunities at lower cost than private alternatives.'

Answerer: graduated ECE 2022. 'Joining MANIT has been one of the best decisions of my life... academics are good compared to other similar NITs, labs are old, new classrooms are nice and the placement is great.' Being in Bhopal gives 'the luxury of joining great coachings for GATE/UPSC/CAT.' 'Students are allowed to bring their own vehicles from second year and there are no hostel timings from second year.'

Answerer: Vaibhav Patwari, CSE (2020). Describes Hostel 10 for freshers: NTB is 1.5km away requiring daily walk/cycling; student store meets 'most necessities'; 'mess serves decent and well balanced meals' but 'you'll soon get bored... begin to dislike it'; sports facilities (TT, badminton, volleyball, cricket) present. Separately, other answers on the same page (not fully captured in accessible snippet) reference: 'Ragging is still prevalent in MANIT, and it is much more serious than any other college' — attributed to a different, unnamed answerer on the same thread; recorded as a distinct data point below.

Unnamed answerer on same Quora-mirrored thread: 'Ragging is still prevalent in MANIT, and it is much more serious than any other college. Those who claim that it is a zero ragging campus, consider ragging to be limited to physical assault. However...' (text truncated in accessible snippet).

known_limitations: This extraction covers only the specific pages/snippets retrieved during this session, not a full crawl of all ~800+ Shiksha reviews or ~165 Careers360 reviews or the full Collegedunia review archive. Item count reflects what was actually read, not the full population.

Some reviews on aggregator sites present run-on/aggregated text blocks (multiple reviewers' snippets concatenated in search results) where individual review boundaries were not always cleanly separable — in such cases each identifiable distinct claim was extracted as its own item where reasonably attributable, but some misattribution risk exists and is flagged via content_access: snippet_only.
review_date is null wherever no explicit date was visible in the retrieved content — dates were not inferred or estimated.

The Collegedunia platform shows two different aggregate rating scales (7.9/10 on the main listing vs. 3.9/5 on an older mirror) that were not reconciled; both reported as observed for backend adjudication.
No numerical sentiment score, aspect score, or confidence label has been generated anywhere in this output, per instruction.
